snippet.title: MAN vs. GARY | New Look Trailer, an idle comedy boss-siege
snippet.description:
There is a monster in the bay. His name is Gary.

You are one man in one small boat with one bow. Gary is roughly the size of a district. This is not a fair fight, and everyone involved knows it, including Gary, who finds the whole thing a little tedious.

So you do the only sensible thing. You row out, you shoot him until you drown, you file the paperwork, and you row out again. Every arrow counts. The damage stays. Gary remembers. And somewhere around your four hundredth drowning, you start to win.

MAN vs. GARY is an idle comedy boss-siege that plays whether you are watching or not, a hand illustrated world where failure is the whole point and the sea monster always dies mid-sentence.

Newly rebuilt, with the whole game redrawn.

▸ Wishlist on Steam:
https://store.steampowered.com/app/5015970/Man_vs_Gary/

Wishlists are how Steam decides whether to show a game to anybody else, so a click now is worth a great deal more than a click on release day.

WHAT YOU ARE IN FOR

Lose, professionally. Death is not a fail state, it is a filing. Every drowning pays out, advances the story, and stamps another Maritime Incident Report. The monster's HP never resets, so your worst day still chipped him.

Idle that respects your time. The crew keeps rowing, shooting and drowning while you are away. Come home to progress, a report, and a monster that has had hours to think about it.

The harbour is the shop. Walk the quay and buy a better bow, a sturdier boat, a crew of sorts (a second guy, a motivational parrot, a man who writes things down) and a grudge that pays interest.

Seven things that want you gone. Gary the kraken. Ignatius, who is on fire and knows it. The Deep Sea Lurker, who is so sorry. Kevin & Kevin, a two headed argument. THE BARONESS, who owns the seabed and resents being involved. THE COMMITTEE, which cannot kill you without a motion. And, after the gym montage, SWOLE GARY.

Retire the Captain. When the wall is too high, hang up the bow and hand the boat to someone angrier. He inherits the grudge, the statue and every way you have died, plus a permanent damage bonus that stacks with every retirement. Retiring is not starting over, it is a promotion, and there is a certificate.

THE DROWNING BOARD. A global leaderboard that ranks the entire world by how many times they have drowned. Aim high.

A game that talks back. Hundreds of lines of deadpan monster commentary, bureaucratic death reports, a Committee that produces one (1) actionable insight, a gentleman gull who would never, and a mandatory tea break observed by both sides.

No microtransactions. No energy timers. Just you, a boat, and a kraken with a grievance.
